gloss: to look after; to take care of

definitions.gloss: to look after; to take care of; to attend to
definitions.explanation: To provide care, supervision, or assistance to someone. Often used for caring for children, elderly family members, or subordinates.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る。
{母|はは}が{入院|にゅういん}している{間|あいだ}、{父|ちち}が{家事|かじ}の{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: While my mother was in the hospital, my father took care of the housework.

examples.japanese: {先輩|せんぱい}がいつも{新人|しんじん}の{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}てくれるので、{職場|しょくば}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}がいい。
examples.english: The senior staff always look after the new employees, so the workplace atmosphere is good.

notes:
USAGE:
A very common expression meaning to care for or look after someone or something. The verb {見|み}る conjugates normally as an ichidan verb. Often used with particles like の or が before {面倒|めんどう}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子|こ}どもの{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る (to look after children)
- {親|おや}の{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る (to look after one's parents)
- {後輩|こうはい}の{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る (to look after junior colleagues)
- {面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}てもらう (to be looked after)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {世話|せわ}をする: to take care of — slightly more formal, can also mean to arrange or mediate
- {介護|かいご}する: to provide nursing care — specifically for elderly or disabled persons
